feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
entry.summary: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

entry.title: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
entry.summary: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

entry.title: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
entry.summary: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

entry.title: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.

entry.title: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over plan to sell public lands to states and tribes
entry.summary: The Trump administration wants to sell some federal public lands to states, local governments and tribes, a plan that's once again drawing swift bi-partisan opposition.

entry.title: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
entry.summary: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.

entry.title: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
entry.summary: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.

entry.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
entry.summary: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

entry.title: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
entry.summary: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

entry.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
entry.summary: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.
